name: News Ticker
description: Displays scrolling news headlines from RSS feeds including sports news from ESPN, NCAA updates, and custom RSS sources
author: ChuckBuilds

versions.notes: global.font_size works. customization.headline_text.font_size (schema default 16) and source_text.font_size (8) were compared against 12 and 6 to decide whether they had been customised, so the merged defaults always counted as a change and a Press Start 2P 16px override replaced global.font_size -- lowering it, as the README advises, did nothing. The comparisons now use the schema defaults, global.font_size's schema default is 16 (what every default install already showed), and a live config save no longer falls back to 12. A config that stores global.font_size 12 (the old schema default, which the web UI wrote on save) keeps drawing headlines at 16px, as it did before: a stored 12 is read as that old default rather than a choice, so those installs do not shrink to a blurry, off-grid 12px. Any other size is used as set; 8 gives smaller headlines. Scroll pacing comes only from the core's resolver (global.display.scroll_speed / scroll_delay): the pre-resolver path is removed, headline paging budgets use the speed the resolver applied rather than the raw ratio, and the dynamic-duration settings (min/max_duration_seconds, buffer_ratio) reach the scroll helper again -- they were applied only on the pre-resolver path. target_fps and background_service.enabled / max_retries / priority were never read: they are kept for compatibility and ignored (still shown in the settings form, marked deprecated), so saved configs that carry them stay valid. Headline pages are sized with a second of headroom under the scroll helper's own duration clamp (and the extra panel width it scrolls), so a full page is not clipped. The ticker releases the scroll state (and its frame hold) while it shows the no-headlines or error message. README: the background-thread and rotation_threshold descriptions are corrected. Requires LEDMatrix core 3.4.0, as before.

Requires LEDMatrix core 3.4.0 or newer, because the ticker uses the new scroll frame pacing. Since #462 (2026-09-07) display() passes frame_hold to display_manager.set_scrolling_state(), an argument core 3.3.x does not have, so on those cores every frame raised TypeError and the ticker stayed blank. The manifest still admitted any core from 2.0.0, so the store kept offering it there. The floor is now 3.4.0 (versions[0] and compatible_versions), so the store refuses the install on an older core and asks the user to update LEDMatrix first. A copy already installed on a 3.3.x core stays broken until that core is updated. No code change.

Saving the config page no longer loses dynamic duration settings. dynamic_duration was typed boolean-or-object, so the web form drew it as a single checkbox and every save replaced the stored object (min/max duration, buffer ratio) with true. It is now a plain object; a legacy true/false is still read by the plugin and becomes the object on the next save. A custom feed logo now needs only a path: the plugin never read the id, and a logo stored without one failed validation on every save.

Load the 4x6 detail face on its 7px pixel grid. 4x6-font rasterises cleanly only at whole multiples of 7; at ppem 6 the 1-bit (fontmode "1") mono rasteriser thresholds every glyph down from 4px wide to 3px, so W/M and 0/8 lose the pixels that tell them apart, and getlength returns a fractional advance whose value depends on the installed FreeType -- two boards on one config measured the same string up to 17% apart. Same grid football-scoreboard keeps in _FONT_PIXEL_GRID. PressStart2P is snapped to its own 8px grid in the same pass. The headline/source font_size defaults move onto PressStart2P's 8px grid (12->16, 6->8).

Stop the web UI's own control reporting the plugin as degraded. feeds.enabled_feeds, the feed picker, renders as a checkbox group, and that widget is saved with a hidden companion field, so using the control writes enabled_feeds_data beside enabled_feeds. The plugin never reads the key, but the feeds object that declares the setting set additionalProperties: false, so the core's schema check flagged it and the web UI showed "Degraded: Config schema: Field 'feeds': Additional properties are not allowed ('enabled_feeds_data' was unexpected)" on a config the UI itself had just written. The key is now permitted -- unconstrained, since the widget has submitted it both as an array and as a JSON string -- while unknown keys are still rejected, so a typo in a hand-edited config is still caught. Same fix as odds-ticker 1.4.5. Affects only the schema; nothing about what the plugin fetches or draws changes.

Make every font in the picker work, and document every setting. Three of the six font faces rendered identically to the default: cozette.bdf has no font file anywhere, and both .bdf faces failed because a bitmap font exists at exactly one pixel size while the loader asked for font_size. Bitmap faces are now loaded at the size the file's PIXEL_SIZE header declares, and cozette.bdf is removed from the pickers -- the same fix already landed for clock-simple, which shared this code. Verified by hashing renders: before, four of six were the same image; after, all five remaining faces are distinct. The README is rewritten around real recorded ESPN headlines and covers all 31 settings, including that a fresh install shows nothing because enabled_feeds is empty by default, and that font_size is the first thing to lower if the ticker reads as a stream of letters rather than a headline.

Keep the rendered ticker when a refresh returns the same headlines. update() discarded the scroll image and the rendered headline images on every refresh regardless of whether anything had changed, and an RSS feed mostly returns what it returned last time. The next Vegas fetch then rebuilt a strip that was still correct: measured on a 512x64 rig at 427ms for a 10220x64 image, on the render thread, which is where the marquee's stutter came from. The discard is now gated on the headline set actually differing. Font, colour and feed-set changes still force a re-render, since those alter the drawing without altering the headlines.

Fix ESPN 403s. Around 2026-08-04 ESPN's site.api began rejecting both browser-style and bare custom User-Agent strings, which returned 403 Forbidden for every request this plugin made. Requests now send an identifying agent with the project URL, which ESPN accepts. No behaviour change beyond the header.

Pixel-perfect text. Every draw surface now sets fontmode = "1" so glyphs render 1-bit instead of anti-aliased. PIL anti-aliases by default, blending glyph edges into dim partial-lit pixels that read as blur on a 1:1 LED matrix; at the default font_size of 12 -- which does not land on Press Start 2P's 8px design grid -- a single headline picked up around 150 of them. Applies to headlines, feed labels, separators and the fallback screens, and to the throwaway surfaces used to measure text, so metrics can never disagree with what renders. Matches the convention already used by ledmatrix-flights and the sports scoreboards.

Headlines no longer get cut off part-way through. The plugin never declared supports_dynamic_duration(), because BasePlugin looks for a top-level dynamic_duration key while this plugin has always kept that block under global -- so the display controller treated the ticker as fixed-duration, never consulted is_cycle_complete(), and cut the strip at a flat wall-clock time no matter how much was left to scroll. Implemented the full hook family (supports_dynamic_duration, get_cycle_duration, get_dynamic_duration_cap, reset_cycle_state) so the controller now holds the display until the strip has actually finished. Added headline paging: each turn carries as many headlines as can finish scrolling in the time available, and the next turn resumes at the first headline that didn't fit, so the tail of a long feed list finally reaches the panel instead of the old rotate-one-headline-every-three-cycles behavior. New global.headline_paging config block (enabled by default).

Config schema reorganized for a clearer setup experience: fine-tuning fields moved behind the web UI's collapsed Advanced Settings section (x-advanced). UX-only; no fields, defaults, or behavior changed.

Fix the "No Feeds Enabled"/"No Headlines Available" fallback message overflowing off the right edge on narrow panels -- it drew at a fixed (5, 12) position with no width check at all. Now truncated to the panel width (with an ellipsis) and centered, matching the fallback pattern used elsewhere in this plugin family. Also brightened the fallback text from a dim (150,150,150) to (220,220,220) for better contrast.
